skill_traces.query:
Evan: Hey Sam, hope you're doing good. Something funny happened last night.
Sam: Hey Evan, what's up? What happened? Let me know.
Evan: Yesterday I went out with my friends and had a bit too much to drink. I ended up doing something I regret and it involved someone's roses.
Sam: What's up with that incident? All good now?
Evan: Oof, Sam, so embarrassing! I had a pee accident near some roses - can you believe it? I'm so sorry about that.
Sam: Uh oh, Evan! That's awkward. Did anyone get mad at you? Are you okay?
Evan: I was so embarrassed when I saw what happened the next morning, so I apologized and luckily they were understanding. Yeah, I was out of control--guess I gotta be more careful next time.
Sam: They were understanding? Phew! We all mess up sometimes, we're human after all.
Evan: Yeah, they were understanding, which was great. But it's a good reminder to be more careful. We all make mistakes, but it's important to learn from them. Speaking of, my partner and I tried snowshoeing this weekend. It was part of a new adventure for us and surprisingly fun.
Sam: Yeah, Evan, you're right. Mistakes happen, but it's good to learn from them. Snowshoeing sounds like a great way to stay active during the winter. I've been thinking and I made a meal plan and workout schedule. I'm getting motivated by something I saw, so starting today I'm gonna do my best to stay on track.
Evan: Good work, Sam! You've got a plan and you're dedicated to staying healthy - have you asked your doctor for advice? They could probably give you even more diet and exercise tips.
Sam: Thanks, Evan! Haven't seen a doctor in a while, but it's probably a good idea to get some advice. I'm going to make an appointment soon.
Evan: What advice are you planning to get from the doctor?
Sam: I'm gonna ask the doc about a balanced diet plan and getting advice on low-impact exercises, given my current situation.
Evan: Sounds good, Sam. That's definitely a step in the right direction. Remember to focus on a balanced diet and low-impact exercises. Let me know how it goes.
Sam: That looks great! Where did you get the idea for this salad? Also, do you have any suggestions for low-impact exercises?
Evan: I got it from a nearby restaurant. As for low-impact exercises, swimming, yoga, and walking are good options.
Sam: The salad idea from a restaurant is a smart move, Evan! And thanks for the exercise tips. Also I watched The Godfather last night, and it motivated me to keep up with my routine. "I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse" - now that's motivation!
Evan: Yoga's definitely a great start, Sam. It's helped me with stress and staying flexible, which is perfect alongside the diet. And yes, The Godfather is a legendary thing to watch, can be re-watched many times!
Sam: Between a healthier diet and yoga, I’m hoping for some positive changes.
Evan:  By the way there are plenty of other low-impact exercises that can be fun. Going on beach sunsets is one of my favorites - good for exercise and totally calming.
Sam: That looks zen. Gonna go for some beach walks - thanks for the tip, Evan! I want to brag, I had that recurring dream again where I'm flying over skyscrapers!
Evan: I think a little more and you'll learn how to control those dreams, once you get the hang of it let me know haha! Enjoy the fresh air and the views. Have fun!
Sam: Thanks Evan! Gonna make the most of it. You too, have a good one!

selected.name: Extract Behavior-Purpose Links
selected.description: Use when a speaker explicitly connects an activity or behavior to a purpose like stress relief, comfort, boredom, or motivation.
content: During extraction, if a speaker links a behavior (eating, exercise, visiting a place, etc.) to a purpose or internal state (stress relief, comfort, motivation), create a memory candidate that records the behavior as a means to that purpose, using memory kind 'preference' or 'event' as appropriate.
Do not let a concurrent emotional state (e.g., guilt) replace this behavior-purpose fact.

During CRUD, when such a preference candidate is present, do not merge or overwrite it with a broader state memory that omits the purpose; preserve the behavior-purpose link unless new evidence contradicts it.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains explicit links between activities (e.g., snowshoeing, yoga, beach walks) and purposes like stress relief, staying active, and motivation, which aligns with the skill's focus on extracting behavior-purpose links.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Goals and Intended Impact
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states a hope, goal, dream, or intended impact for an activity or interest.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly states a user's goal, hope, aspiration, or intended impact for an activity (e.g., share stories, make a difference, reach others), capture it as a separate facet in the memory content; do not replace it with only current emotional benefits like escape, expression, or healing.
When enriching an existing memory, preserve previously stored facets and ADD the newly stated goal or impact rather than overwriting the memory with a narrower paraphrase.
Stop after capturing the explicit goal and its immediate context; do not enumerate every possible future hope or infer unstated ambitions.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Suggestions
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message contains explicit advice, suggestions, or recommendations from one participant to another, extract them as memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, suggestions, and recommendations as memory-worthy. Capture the advisor, the recipient, the advised action, and the source message.
Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.
Represent as an event or relationship memory; create at most one candidate per distinct piece of advice.
Stop after capturing the stated advice; do not infer outcomes or expand into related topics.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Concrete Activity from Follow-Up Clarification
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message describes an activity vaguely and the next message names the concrete result.
content: During extraction, treat any message reporting the speaker performing an activity as a candidate source, even when the object is only a photo or pronoun.
If the following message from another participant identifies the concrete object or result, extract an event memory capturing who did what, using both messages as evidence.
Do not skip follow-up messages that clarify or name an earlier activity.
